subject: Clarify assignment vs. license for productization — MSA/Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Kate Evans <kate.evans@cloudwave.com>, procurement@cloudwave.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify assignment vs. license for productization — MSA/Order Form redlines

Hi Kate + Cloudwave procurement team,

Thanks for the quick review and for the redlines — we have them and appreciate the clear markers in the PDF. Two specific items surfaced on our side that I want to make sure we align on before we route final language to Legal:

1) Output ownership vs. assignment: Cloudwave’s redline suggests an assignment of productized outputs in the Order Form. We generally offer a carveout for customer data and derived customer-specific models, but we avoid broad assignment of platform IP (service improvements, models trained by Redwood on aggregated signals). Can you confirm whether you need exclusive assignment of the deliverables or a paid license sufficient for productization?

2) Feedback license scope: your team marked our Feedback License as "perpetual, irrevocable" and added language to allow downstream commercialization. We want to permit operational use of feedback for improvements with appropriate safeguards (no re-use of raw customer content beyond anonymized signals) — we think a narrowly scoped license (defined by purpose and exclusions) will get you the controls you need without assignment.

Attached: Redwood_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (our consolidated redlines), OrderForm_Cloudwave_marked.docx (Cloudwave’s marked Order Form).

Proposed next steps:
- Kate, can you indicate whether Cloudwave requires assignment (absolute transfer of title) for the outputs listed in the Order Form, or whether a transferable exclusive license is acceptable?
- Rishi / Laura, I’m looping you for Legal/RevOps review. If Cloudwave expects assignment, we’ll need to escalate and propose a limited-scope assignment or substitute commercial terms (fee/escrow).

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (annotated), OrderForm_Cloudwave_marked.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kate Evans <kate.evans@cloudwave.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify assignment vs. license for productization — MSA/Order Form redlines

Thanks Rachel. Quick internal alignment note:

- Product/Legal perspective: Redwood’s standard position is that customers own their input and the direct output derived solely from their data (e.g., user records exported verbatim, one-off generated artifacts explicitly delivered). We do not assign model weights or platform-level IP — instead, we grant a license to use outputs for internal and productization purposes.

- Commercial fallback: if the customer insists on assignment, we can offer a narrow assignment for specific, identifiable deliverables (e.g., a named dataset or a generated model snapshot) subject to an additional fee and escrow. This keeps platform IP protected.

Action for Kate/Cloudwave: if you can list the specific outputs you want assigned (by Exhibit or Order Form line item), we can draft precise language. Otherwise, Laura and I will propose alternative license language that supports productization while preserving Redwood’s core IP.

—Rishi
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify assignment vs. license for productization — MSA/Order Form redlines

Rachel / Rishi — thanks for the summary. A couple points from Cloudwave Legal / Procurement: 

1) Why assignment: Cloudwave’s product team plans to incorporate Redwood-generated artifacts directly into their SaaS tenant and redistribute certain outputs to downstream OEM partners. They prefer assignment to avoid later title disputes and to keep our product roadmap flexible.

2) Narrow ask: they are willing to limit the assignment request to a set of deliverables if we can define them concretely in the Order Form (e.g., "custom NLP model trained only on Cloudwave inputs, final labeled dataset export v1.2").

3) Feedback license: Cloudwave cannot accept a perpetual, broad license that allows Redwood to commercialize feedback-derived models that include Cloudwave proprietary signals. They need assurances that (a) raw proprietary content will not be reused to train models exposed to third parties, and (b) any derivatives used for broader model improvement will be aggregative and de-identified.

Attached is our summary redline and a short memo from product describing the outgoing deliverables. We can accept an exclusive, transferable license limited to the named deliverables if that helps avoid a full assignment.

Please confirm whether Redwood can: (1) narrow the Feedback License to exclude Cloudwave proprietary content from any external model training; and (2) provide a mechanism (fee/escrow or limited-scope assignment) for the specific deliverables listed in Exhibit A.

Thanks — Kate
Kate Evans
Senior Counsel, Cloudwave Systems
kate.evans@cloudwave.com

Attachments: Cloudwave_redlines_summary.pdf, Cloudwave_product_memo.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kate Evans <kate.evans@cloudwave.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify assignment vs. license for productization — MSA/Order Form redlines

Thanks Kate — good, pragmatic framing. Proposal from our side to unblock:

1) Feedback license amendment (short form):
"Company Feedback" means Customer-provided information, usage signals, and annotations. Redwood may use Company Feedback solely to improve the Services for Customer and to improve aggregated models provided that (i) Customer Confidential Information is not used to train models made available to third parties, and (ii) any model improvements derived from Company Feedback are de‑identified and aggregated such that they do not contain Customer Confidential Information in a reversible form.

2) Deliverable assignment / license:
- If Cloudwave requires assignment for specific items listed in Exhibit A, Redwood will grant assignment of title to those enumerated deliverables in exchange for a one-time assignment fee and placement of a model snapshot or dataset in escrow. For all other outputs, Redwood grants a perpetual, royalty-free, transferable license to use, reproduce, and distribute outputs for productization.

3) Execution plan:
- Rachel / Rishi: I recommend we circulate the precise Exhibit A naming the deliverables (product to confirm exact artifacts).
- Kate: if Cloudwave agrees to the Exhibit A + fee/escrow compromise, Laura Legal can prepare redline language for the Order Form and an escrow schedule.

I’ll draft the language above into a short amendment and share a PR in Drive.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & RevOps, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
